messages.subject: digit.fixed surface file issue
parts:
Dear Geomorph group, 

After many analyses using geomorph on landmark datasets collected using other programs, I decided to try collecting 3D landmarks with geomorph in R. I produced a .ply surface of a bone, used read.ply() to load it into R, then used digit.fixed() to collect a few fixed landmark points. When placing points, they do not seem to "stick" to the surface closest to the screen. Instead, the red points are seen within the bone on what I believe are other parts of the complex surface. Does anyone have suggestions about how to process .ply files before loading them into R to avoid this issue? Is there a software that tends to produce more appropriate .ply files for geomorph landmark digitization? I suppose the issue may have to do with rgl and very little to do with geomorph functions themselves, but any advice is appreciated. 

Thanks, 
Chris Percival
Anthropology
Stony Brook University

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] digit.fixed surface file issue
parts:
Chris,

 

Yes that can be a bit persnickety. What is happening here is that you are selecting a point on the surface that has no data (recall a surface is a cloud of points, but it is represented as a mesh of polygons in-between them). If you select a place on the mesh in between the actual xyz points, it will sometimes pass through the object and find a close point below.

 

Zooming in more on the location on the surface can often help with this.

 

Dean
